passage: I'm Devika, and my brother Chinmay is eight. At Tanya's birthday party he had two pieces of cake, a fistful of toffees and a fizzy drink. For an hour he was everywhere, jumping off the sofa arms, shouting, spinning till he fell over. Then, around six, it was like someone had pulled his plug. He sat in a corner rubbing his eyes, and cried when I said it was time to go. At home he snapped at Mummy about his shoes. I don't really know what was going on inside him. Mummy didn't lecture or ban sweets. Before the next party she gave him a proper dal-rice lunch, and there he had one piece of cake. He was still bouncy, but there was no crying in corners.

qa.q: What did Chinmay have at Tanya's party?
qa.a: Chinmay had two pieces of cake, a fistful of toffees and a fizzy drink.

qa.q: What might Chinmay's crying in the corner suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Chinmay was tired and cranky after the burst of energy, though Devika could not know for sure.

qa.q: What did Mummy change for the next party, and why is it wiser than a ban?
qa.a: Mummy gave Chinmay a proper lunch first and he had one piece of cake, which kept his mood steadier without making sweets forbidden.

qa.q: What was the party like for Devika to watch?
qa.a: Devika watched Chinmay go from spinning everywhere to crying in a corner, and seemed puzzled by the sudden change.

grounding: A child after lots of sweets seems hyper, then tired and irritable, and a proper meal with a treat in moderation keeps his mood steadier.

Week one. Every day Pradeep's tiffin held sweet biscuits and a packet of jelly sweets. By eleven he was drumming on the desk and chatting nonstop. By twelve he was yawning, head on his arms, snapping at anyone who spoke to him. Zainab Ma'am noticed the pattern.
Week two. She mentioned it gently to his father at pickup, without blame. "Nothing needs banning," she said. "Maybe something filling alongside?" His father nodded; he had noticed the evening grumps too.
Week four. Pradeep's tiffin now held a paratha with paneer, some fruit and one biscuit as a treat. At twelve he was still upright, finishing his sums, and he laughed when he got one wrong instead of throwing his pencil.

qa.q: What was in Pradeep's tiffin in week four?
qa.a: A paratha with paneer, some fruit and one biscuit as a treat.

qa.q: How was Pradeep feeling by twelve in week one?
qa.a: Pradeep felt tired and irritable, yawning with his head on his arms and snapping at others.

qa.q: Why was Zainab Ma'am's suggestion helpful?
qa.a: She suggested adding something filling without banning anything, so Pradeep's father could change the tiffin without feeling blamed.

qa.q: What had Pradeep's father noticed at home?
qa.a: Pradeep's father had noticed the evening grumps too.

grounding: A child's energy spikes and crashes after sweets, and a more balanced tiffin with one treat keeps his mood steadier.

passage:
'Mumma! Mumma! Watch me jump off the sofa! Again! Again!'
'Ojas, you've been bouncing since we got back from Aryan's party.'
'I had four cupcakes and a candy bag!'
An hour later, Gurleen found him face down on the rug.
'Ojas? Homework time.'
'I don't WANT to. I'm tired. Everything's boring.' He kicked the rug and started to cry.
Gurleen sat beside him. 'Remember how you felt at the party? Like a rocket?'
'Yeah.'
'And now?'
'Like a flat balloon.'
'Sugar can do that. Up like a rocket, then down with a bump.' She stroked his hair. 'Tomorrow, before Riya's party, let's have proper dal-rice lunch first. Then you can have a cupcake or two there.'
Ojas sniffed. 'I can still have cake?'
'Of course. Just not only cake.'

qa.q: How many cupcakes did Ojas eat at the party?
qa.a: Four cupcakes.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling an hour after the party?
qa.a: He felt tired, cranky and bored, crying and kicking the rug.

qa.q: Why is Gurleen's plan wiser than banning sweets?
qa.a: A proper meal first keeps his energy steadier, and still allowing some cake avoids making sweets forbidden or a battle.

qa.q: How might Gurleen have felt finding Ojas face down on the rug?
qa.a: She was probably tired and a bit worried, but understood the crash rather than scolding.

grounding: Shows a child hyper after sweets and then irritable and tired as energy drops, and a parent choosing a proper meal plus treats in moderation over banning.

passage: On Diwali that year, I ate sweets all day. Kaju katli at breakfast, gulab jamun at lunch, laddoos with every visitor. By afternoon I was racing round the terrace with my cousin Trisha, shrieking and knocking things over. Then, around five, it was like someone switched me off. I felt heavy and grumpy, and when Amma asked me to finish my holiday homework, I burst into tears over one sum. I'm Yamini, and I remember Amma sitting beside me and saying, 'Your body went up too high and came down too fast.' The next festival, she didn't ban sweets. She just made sure I had a proper meal first, dal and sabzi, and one or two sweets after. I still raced around the terrace. But I didn't crash into tears.

qa.q: What sweets did Yamini eat at lunch?
qa.a: Gulab jamun.

qa.q: How did Yamini feel around five o'clock?
qa.a: Yamini felt heavy, grumpy and tearful, bursting into tears over one sum.

qa.q: What did Amma change at the next festival?
qa.a: She did not ban sweets but made sure Yamini had a proper meal first, then one or two sweets after.

qa.q: How might Trisha have experienced the afternoon of racing around?
qa.a: Trisha probably found it wild and fun at first, then was surprised when Yamini suddenly crashed.

grounding: Shows a child hyper after too many sweets and then tired and tearful as energy drops, and a parent choosing balanced meals and moderate treats over banning.

Note to Nazia's parents, Class 3
I've noticed a pattern on the days Nazia buys sweets from the canteen at break. For about half an hour she is very excitable: running in the corridor, talking over others, unable to sit. Then, by the last period, she is tired, tearful and irritable, and she struggled with her reading today. On days she has her lunch box from home, she seems steadier. I'm not suggesting a ban on treats; she enjoys them, and that's fine. Perhaps a filling breakfast and a packed snack like chana or fruit, with the canteen sweet saved for Fridays, might help her energy last the day. Happy to talk.
Anand, class teacher

qa.q: What does Nazia buy from the canteen at break?
qa.a: Sweets.

qa.q: How does Nazia seem to feel by the last period on sweet days?
qa.a: She seems tired, tearful and irritable.

qa.q: What does Anand suggest instead of a ban?
qa.a: A filling breakfast, a packed snack like chana or fruit, and saving the canteen sweet for Fridays.

qa.q: How might Nazia's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They may feel grateful for the observation and relieved that the teacher is not asking them to ban treats.

grounding: Shows a teacher noticing a child's hyper spell after sweets and later tiredness and irritability, and suggesting balanced food and moderate treats rather than a ban.

passage:
Saturday
Dear Diary, it was Vijay's birthday party and I ate cake, two laddoos, green jelly and a whole packet of toffees. For one hour I was a rocket. I ran round the building three times and screamed on the swing. Then at six I felt like a flat balloon. My head hurt, I shouted at Vijay when he wanted the swing, and I cried because my shoe was tied wrong. Mummy didn't say "no more sweets ever". She gave me dal-rice and curd for dinner and said tomorrow the sweets can come after lunch, not instead of it. I felt better after eating. I said sorry to Vijay on the phone.
Reena

qa.q: What did Mummy give Reena for dinner?
qa.a: Mummy gave Reena dal-rice and curd.

qa.q: How was Reena feeling at six o'clock, and what shows it?
qa.a: Reena felt tired and irritable, like a flat balloon; the headache, shouting at Vijay and crying over a shoe show it.

qa.q: What was sensible about Mummy's plan for sweets?
qa.a: Instead of banning sweets, Mummy kept them for after a proper meal, which keeps energy and mood steadier.

qa.q: How might Vijay have felt when Reena shouted at him on his birthday?
qa.a: Vijay was probably hurt and confused, since he only wanted a turn on the swing at his own party.

grounding: Illustrates a child going hyper after sweets and then irritable and tired, with a balanced meal and treats after food keeping mood steadier than a ban.
